sn16.4:1.3: what kind of bhikkhu is worthy to be a visitor of families, and what kind of bhikkhu is not worthy to be a visitor of families?”
sn16.4:1.4: “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One….”
sn16.4:2.1: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might approach families with the thought:
sn16.4:2.2: ‘May they give to me, not hold back!
sn16.4:2.3: May they give me much, not a little!
sn16.4:2.4: May they give me fine things, not shabby things!
sn16.4:2.5: May they give me promptly, not slowly!
sn16.4:2.6: May they give me considerately, not casually!’
sn16.4:2.7: When a bhikkhu approaches families with such a thought, if they do not give, he thereby becomes hurt; on that account he experiences pain and displeasure.
sn16.4:2.8: If they give little rather than much …
sn16.4:2.9: If they give shabby things rather than fine things …
sn16.4:2.10: If they give slowly rather than promptly …
sn16.4:2.11: If they give casually rather than considerately, he thereby becomes hurt; on that account he experiences pain and displeasure.
sn16.4:2.12: Such a bhikkhu is not worthy to be a visitor of families.
sn16.4:3.1: “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might approach families with the thought:
sn16.4:3.2: ‘When among others’ families, how could I possibly think:
sn16.4:3.5: “May they give to me, not hold back!…
sn16.4:3.7: May they give me respectfully, not casually!”?’
sn16.4:3.8: When a bhikkhu approaches families with such a thought, if they do not give …
sn16.4:3.9: if they give casually rather than considerately,
sn16.4:3.10: he does not thereby become hurt;
sn16.4:3.12: he does not on that account experience pain and displeasure.
sn16.4:3.13: Such a bhikkhu is worthy to be a visitor of families.
sn16.4:4.1: “Bhikkhus, Kassapa approaches families with such a thought….
sn16.4:4.4: Thus if they do not give …
sn16.4:4.7: if they give casually rather than considerately,
sn16.4:4.9: he does not thereby become hurt;
sn16.4:4.12: he does not on that account experience pain and displeasure.
sn16.4:4.13: “Bhikkhus, I will exhort you by the example of Kassapa or one who is similar to Kassapa. Being exhorted, you should practise accordingly.”
